IT-related professional certifications.
High School diploma or GED equivalent.
Associates Degree with an emphasis in a computer-related field OR equivalent combination of work experience and coursework.
Minimum one (1)year experience in a customer service-related field. Tenacity in troubleshooting and resolving problems.
Experience in public sector IT environment.
Primary responsibility is user support and customer service. Be present, visible and available to users requiring technical assistance.

Responds verbally to questions from callers and walk-ins; remotely assist students, staff, and faculty with technology problems in offices, classrooms, and assist in person with problems in the computer labs.

Learns fundamental operations of commonly used software, hardware, and other equipment. Support the district’s audio, visual, lighting, teleconferencing, and technical needs for instruction, classrooms, events and meetings.
Follows standard Help Desk operating procedures; accurately log all Help Desk contacts using Help Desk tracking software.
Maintains computer labs desktops and classroom technology.
Attends all Help Desk training sessions.
Becomes familiar with available help resources; stay updated on campus technology changes and problems.
Becomes familiar with the Palo Verde Community College District’s policies, services, and staff.
Assists in training and mentoring student workers.
Directs calls and helpdesk tickets to appropriate IT staff as necessary.

Performs a variety of minor network problem analysis and monitoring tasks for the Information Technology Help Desk; monitor IT network management systems and respond appropriately to user requests and problems; perform initial problem analysis and triage problem to IT technical staff when appropriate.
Compiles data and prepare reports setting forth progress, adverse trends and appropriate recommendations based on information from the help desk system.

Participates in the preparation of procedure manuals and documentation for help desk use; conduct periodic user satisfaction surveys and track user problem trends; make recommendations for improvements to the network systems and create reports based on information provided from user surveys and trends.

Participates in the creation and distribution of network related information to users to include information such as help desk procedures, IT department newsletter and network/desktop handbooks and How-To documents.
Assists in the development of a comprehensive training plan for help desk procedures; assist in training personnel providing backup coverage.

Assists in on-site installations of network systems for users, which require the ability to see, bend, reach, reach overhead, squat, kneel, crawl under desks and in tight spaces, and manual dexterity to connect intricate wiring.
Requires a variable work schedule which will include late evening shifts and weekends at times.
Requires driving to off-campus work sites.

Assists with purchasing paperwork, renewals and maintenance contracts, departmental communications, file storage and organization both paper and electronic, maintains software library and other clerical functions.
Escalates complex or unresolved issues to appropriate IT staff following department protocols.
Assists in identifying technology barriers that may limit access for students or employees with disabilities or limited digital literacy.
Demonstrates a strong commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility principles in all aspects of job performance; actively promotes and creates a welcoming and inclusive environment.
Maintains awareness of emerging best practices in digital accessibility, equity in technology, and culturally responsive support models.
Performs other duties, related to the position, as assigned.
Basic computer hardware, operating systems, and standard office software.
Work effectively in a fast-paced, multi-tasking environment.
Sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, ethnic, racial, age, national origin, religious, gender, sexual orientation, disabilities, and socio-economic backgrounds.
Helpdesk support procedures and ticketing systems.
Follow established procedures and escalate issues when necessary.
Classroom and lab technologies, including AV systems, projectors, etc.
Work responsibly with or without direct supervision.
Network fundamentals and troubleshooting basics.
Learn new technologies and adapt quickly to changes.
College policies, student services, and general IT practices.
Organize tasks and prioritize requests based on urgency and impact.
Learning Management Systems, the District’s online registration system, HTML, FTP programs, Adobe products.
Maintain Confidentiality and handle sensitive information responsibly.
Principles of customer service and user support.
Work independently and collaboratively within a team.
Audio/visual equipment setup and support.
Communicate clearly and professionally with users of varying technical skill levels.
